title: Building a repeatable production investigation workflow
description: Create a systematic approach for investigating and resolving production issues.

data.text: Ad-hoc troubleshooting works for simple problems, but production incidents require a repeatable workflow. A workflow is a sequence of steps you follow every time, regardless of the specific symptom. It ensures you do not miss critical checks, it speeds up resolution, and it creates a record you can refine after the incident.

This lesson brings together all the tools and concepts from the module into a practical framework. You will learn how to triage an incident, gather evidence, form a hypothesis, test it, and document the resolution.

items: Triage: understand the scope and severity of the issue
Gather evidence: collect logs, metrics, and process state
Form a hypothesis: identify the most likely cause
Test the hypothesis: make a safe, reversible change
Confirm resolution: verify the symptom is gone

data.text: Triage means quickly understanding what is broken and who is affected. Is the whole system down or just one service? Is it one user or all users? Is data being lost or just delayed? Severity determines how fast you need to act and whether you need to escalate.

Evidence is data that helps you confirm or reject hypotheses. Start with the system state: what processes are running, what ports are open, and what the CPU and memory look like. Then collect logs: recent errors from application and system logs. Capture timestamps so you can correlate events.

data.code:
# Capture a snapshot of system state
ps aux --sort=-%cpu | head -20 > /tmp/snapshot.txt
ss -tulnp > /tmp/ports.txt
free -h > /tmp/memory.txt
df -h > /tmp/disk.txt
# Capture recent errors
tail -n 200 /var/log/app/error.log > /tmp/errors.txt

data.title: Take snapshots before you change anything
data.text: Never skip the evidence-gathering step. If you restart a service before collecting logs and process state, you may destroy the evidence you need to find the root cause. Snapshots are cheap and fast; root cause analysis without them is hard.

Based on the evidence, form a hypothesis. The hypothesis should be specific enough to test: If the database connection pool is exhausted, restarting the app should temporarily restore connections. If the disk is full, freeing space should restore writes. Test one change at a time and observe the result.

After the issue is resolved, write a short summary. What was the symptom? What was the root cause? What did you do to fix it? What can you do to prevent it from happening again? This turns a painful incident into institutional knowledge.

items: What was the symptom and when did it start?
What evidence proved the root cause?
What can we monitor or alert to catch this earlier?
What can we automate to prevent recurrence?

data.title: Key Takeaways
items: A repeatable workflow reduces mean time to resolution
Always gather evidence before making changes
Test one change at a time and observe the effect
Post-incident reviews turn incidents into improvements
Automate checks and alerts to catch problems earlier
